clue.text: Following attack, lover carries torch

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
to lam is to thrash or set upon someone
a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: After an assault, a jilted suitor still holds a flame for the one he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries torch' reads as pining for someone, but 'torch' is the definition and 'carries' only links the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming brand of the kind carried in processions, which is a torch.

clue.text: Sequence of musical notes in show

definitions.meaning: F, A, C, A, D and E are all names of notes in the scale
a false front or outward pretence

explanation.definitionFit: The letters are six notes of the scale in a row, and a facade is a deceptive outward appearance put on for display.

clue.text: Where fag ends up missing Henry, being lost

indicators.note: missing says the letter for Henry is dropped

parts.note: a fag is British slang for a cigarette, and its stub ends in a tray for ash
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A cigarette ends up somewhere without Henry, who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fag' is British slang for a cigarette; 'fag ends' also suggests stubs. H is the henry, a unit in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means wandering off the right path, so missing or mislaid.

clue.text: Cheese with fine, odd character gets paper container

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a case is an eccentric person, as in 'he's a real case'

explanation.surface: A cheese eater with a fine, eccentric personality is given a paper holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd character' looks like a strange letter but means an eccentric, a 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag for carrying documents.

clue.text: George in secret plan to undermine working alone?

annotationWithheld.why: George in secret plan to undermine working alone? as held: AUTOMATIC (working alone) over PILOT needs an I inside PLOT (secret plan) that no clue word supplies; a word such as 'I' or 'one' seems lost from the OCR and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: George in secret plan to undermine working alone?

clue.text: Call central Angus in a farewell message?

indicators.note: in tells us the middle letters sit inside the farewell message

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the farewell carved on headstones

indicators.note: central asks for the letters at the heart of the word Angus, without its ends

explanation.surface: A phone call to someone in the Scottish county of Angus ends with a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus is a Scottish county. 'farewell message?' looks like part of the definition, but it is the container, the words on a headstone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring up someone is to telephone them, which is to call.

clue.text: Children's paper with leader censored

indicators.note: leader censored means the first letter of the paper is cut out

parts.note: tissue is thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A children's newspaper has its editor's column cut by the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Children stands for 'is'. 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring, as in 'died without issue'.

clue.text: Soldier to employ on behalf of European -Garibaldi, say

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
to use is to employ
pp, per procurationem, is written when signing on behalf of someone

explanation.surface: A soldier is hired on behalf of a European, such as a famous general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garibaldi, say' points to the Italian patriot's first name, so the definition is an example of a person named this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian unifier Garibaldi had this forename, so he is one bearer of the name.

clue.text: Tough troop raised a stink making fuel

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a tough soldier

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the stink is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A hard paratrooper caused an uproar while fuelling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised a stink' reads as complaining loudly, but 'raised' turns NIFF (British slang for a smell) upwards and 'a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin, also called kerosene, is an oil burned in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Miller's tale that has global circulation

definitions.meaning: a novel by the American writer Henry Miller
a line of latitude runs right round the Earth

explanation.surface: A miller's story is read all over the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miller's tale' suggests Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, but it is Henry Miller's 1934 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Miller wrote a novel of this title, and the line of latitude north of the equator circles the whole world.

clue.text: Herb's a cool guy with lots of money

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a hip, cool fellow
a mint is a huge sum, as in 'made a mint'

explanation.surface: A herb is described as a hip, wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Herb stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is the aromatic plant cats love, a herb of the nettle family.

clue.text: Mayday participant, perhaps, runs round copper in several directions

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: round says the directions surround the copper

parts.note: E, S, E and R are east, south, east and right, all directions
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone at a May Day festival is running around a policeman in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mayday' is the distress call, not the spring festival; whoever answers it is a lifeboatman or similar. R for right counts as a direction alongside the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone responding to a distress call is one who saves people in danger, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Very small diamonds taken by angry female after male's done a bunk

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: doing a bunk is British slang for running off, so the letter for male leaves

parts.note: warm can mean heated or angry, as in a warm exchange
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Gems are taken by a furious woman after her man has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done a bunk' (British slang for running away) removes M from WARM F, leaving WARF after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarf as an adjective describes a plant or animal much smaller than normal, so tiny.

clue.text: Type of rag that's used in a national flag

definitions.meaning: a rag is a piece of ragtime music, and Scott Joplin wrote a famous one named after a tree's foliage
Canada's flag carries a red emblem of a leaf at its centre

explanation.surface: A scrap of cloth is cut up to make a country's banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' looks like cloth for a flag, but it is ragtime: Joplin's 1899 Maple Leaf Rag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maple Leaf Rag is a ragtime piece, and the red leaf of that tree is the emblem on Canada's banner.

clue.text: Bill appearing in strange film, not quite topical, that's already been done

indicators.note: appearing in puts the bill inside the jumbled letters
strange says the following letters are scrambled
not quite drops the final letter of the word topical

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An invoice turns up for an odd movie that is slightly behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' jumbles the film words into FAITCOMPLI; 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A fait accompli is a thing settled before anyone could object, a done deal.

clue.text: Unexpected additional runs causing defeat

definitions.meaning: in cricket, extra runs scored when a fielder's throw misses the stumps and runs on
a downfall or toppling of a ruler

explanation.surface: Surprise extra runs lead to a team losing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from a wild return throw are an overthrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for bonus runs off a stray throw, and also the toppling of a government or ruler.

clue.text: Money stopped by king following postponed delivery

indicators.note: following says the money and king pieces come after the postponed word

parts.note: an event that is off has been called off or put back

indicators.note: stopped means cut short, so the last letter of the money word is lost

parts.note: bread is slang for money
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Cash was withheld by a king after a late delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' is a cricket ball, not the post. 'stopped' docks BREAD to BREA.
explanation.definitionFit: An off break is a ball a spin bowler makes turn from the off side, a type of bowled ball.

clue.text: Environs of London consumed by a blaze between dusk and dawn

indicators.note: consumed by says the outskirts are swallowed up inside the blaze

parts.note: light is a blaze of illumination, as in 'set a light'

indicators.note: environs are the outskirts, so take the first and last letters of London

explanation.surface: The outskirts of London were swallowed by a fire that raged through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' suits the fire picture but is the container signal; 'a blaze' splits into the article and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-night lasts the whole night, through the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Drink given by fleet officer at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A naval officer of the fleet hands over a drink while afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' suits the naval picture but signals that FLEET OFFICER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Filter coffee is a brew made by dripping water through grounds, a hot beverage.

clue.text: Dessert, just a small amount

definitions.meaning: a pudding of sponge, custard and cream
a tiny bit, as in 'a ... too much'

explanation.definitionFit: The layered British pudding shares its name with a word for something of little worth or quantity.

clue.text: Vessel by spit receiving interference with service

indicators.note: receiving says the spit piece takes on the service word next to it

parts.note: gob is British slang for spittle
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed

explanation.surface: A tennis serve is disrupted next to some spittle.
explanation.walkthrough: A let in tennis is a serve to be retaken after touching the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a stemmed drinking cup, a vessel for wine.

clue.text: Vitamin 1 taken by friend that's usually fine?

parts.note: B is a vitamin, as in vitamin B
the figure 1 is written out as a word
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A vitamin pill is taken by a pal who is generally in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate. 'fine' means delicate porcelain here, not healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is translucent porcelain, nearly always the delicate tableware sort called fine china.

clue.text: Just about to list

parts.note: C, circa, is the abbreviation for about
to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A ship is on the point of tilting over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' looks like one phrase meaning nearly, but 'Just' is the definition and 'about' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as an adverb means completely or entirely, as in 'clean forgot' or 'just forgot'.

clue.text: It's designed to speed up fish with no tail

indicators.note: with no tail removes the final letter of the fish

parts.note: a turbot is a large flatfish

explanation.surface: Something built to go faster is a fish without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbo, a turbocharger, forces extra air into an engine to boost power and acceleration.

clue.text: Artist, when rejected, caught queen's piercing stare

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
piercing says the caught and queen letters go inside the stare

parts.note: to ogle is to stare lecherously
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: An artist was turned down when the queen caught him leering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' makes OCERGLE, which 'rejected' turns round. 'when' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, a famous painter.

clue.text: Thorough judge gets caught in a net

indicators.note: caught in says the judge is held within the net

parts.note: a caul is a close-fitting net, such as a hairnet or the membrane round a newborn
a ref, referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A meticulous referee ends up trapped in netting.
explanation.walkthrough: A caul is a net cap, or the membrane sometimes found over a newborn's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful means taking pains over details, so painstaking.

clue.text: Compound you'd partly take to Newcastle

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A substance is one you might bring along when travelling to Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'you'd', which belongs to the indicator phrase 'you'd partly take'; the definition is just 'Compound'. 'take to Newcastle' echoes coals to Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketones are a class of organic chemicals, acetone being the best known.

clue.text: Hector's wife stopping a naughty boy pinching medal

indicators.note: pinching says the naughty boy grips what follows inside him

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the wife sits inside the medal

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, worn as a medal

explanation.surface: Hector's wife stops a naughty boy who is stealing a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' is not a name but a verb, with 's for 'is'. The OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully with blustering, so to intimidate someone into compliance.
